title: Cohort Normalization, Dose-Response Curves, and Statistical Comparisons
text: 3D patient-derived cancer models stained nuclear, tumor, apoptotic markers (Labrosse et al., 2024, doi:10.1016/j.xpro.2024.103274), image contains: Viable target/cancer cells (e.g., E-Cadherin positive), decrease drug concentration increases. Dying/apoptotic cells (e.g., cCASP3 positive double-positive E-Cadherin cCASP3), increase drug concentration increases. non-target cells (e.g., onlyDAPIPositve stromal/immune cells), excluded cancer-specific denominator. quantify -target drug sensitivity estimate IC50, drugsens lets specify dead/dying cell marker(s) (dead_markers) viable/total target cell marker(s) (viable_markers total_markers), along control condition (control_treatment_name): Target Cell Viability = 1 - (Dead Cells / Total Target Cells) = Viable Target Cells / (Viable Target Cells + Dead Cells) normalize_to_control() expresses well’s target cell viability percentage matched patient Control mean (pct_of_control, Control = 100%), enabling: Side--side inspection control normalization (plot_normalization_before_after()). Dose-response curve fitting via LOESS 4-parameter log-logistic (4pl) Hill models single-marker multi-marker consensus IC50 estimation (plot_dose_response()). Multi-drug multi-patient cohort summaries (plot_dose_response_heatmap(), plot_treatment_summary(), plot_patient_heatmap()).

title: Cohort Normalization, Dose-Response Curves, and Statistical Comparisons

what: 5. Customizing Plots with drugsens_theme() and drugsens_palette
title: Cohort Normalization, Dose-Response Curves, and Statistical Comparisons
text: drugsens_theme() colorblind-safe drugsens_palette exported can build custom visualizations (comparing patient’s consensus IC50) match rest drugsens report:
code: ic50_df <- attr(p_multi, "consensus_ic50")  ggplot(ic50_df, aes(x = PID, y = ic50, fill = PID, color = PID)) +   geom_col(width = 0.42, alpha = 0.82, color = NA) +   geom_point(size = 3.4, shape = 21, color = "#fcfcfb", stroke = 0.6) +   geom_text(     aes(label = sprintf("%.1f uM", ic50)),     vjust = -0.8,     fontface = "bold",     size = 4.0,     color = "#0b0b0b"   ) +   scale_fill_manual(values = unname(drugsens_palette)) +   scale_color_manual(values = unname(drugsens_palette)) +   scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +   labs(     title = "Consensus Paclitaxel IC50 by Patient",     subtitle = "Calculated directly from the package dataset (E-Cadherin viable vs. cCASP3 + E-Cadherin/cCASP3 dead)",     x = "Patient ID",     y = "Consensus IC50 (uM)"   ) +   drugsens_theme() +   theme(     panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),     legend.position = "none"   )

title: End-to-End Quality Control and Feature Inspection
text: normalizing drug responses fitting dose-response models, critical verify cell segmentation, marker classification, replicate fields view (series) behaved consistently across microscopy screen. tutorial demonstrates complete quality control (QC) workflow drugsens: Auditing per-image total cell counts (sum_cells) marker ratios make_count_dataframe(). Visualizing patient-level marker positivity distributions testing treatments Control get_QC_plots(). Comparing marker ratios across tissue origins drug concentrations get_QC_plots_parsed_merged_data(). Inspecting single-cell morphological features (nuclear area marker intensity) directly data_binding().

title: QuPath Setup and Filename Metadata Conventions
text: key strength drugsens eliminates manual spreadsheet curation: experimental metadata (patient ID, tissue origin, experiment date, sample collection date, single combination drug names, concentrations, units, replicate status) automatically parsed Image column exported QuPath. guide walks : Generating QuPath Groovy export script (generate_qupath_script()). Structuring image filenames single drugs, drug combinations, vehicle controls. Testing filename metadata extraction directly R (string_parsing()). Configuring cell marker relabeling (make_run_config()).

what: 1. Generating and Running the QuPath Groovy Scripts
title: QuPath Setup and Filename Metadata Conventions
text: Run generate_qupath_script() R create ready--use Groovy export template (script_for_qupath.txt):
code: library(drugsens)  out_dir <- tempdir() generate_qupath_script(output_dir = out_dir)  script_lines <- readLines(file.path(out_dir, "script_for_qupath.txt")) cat( paste(head(script_lines, 25), collapse = "\n") ) #>  #> //This code script was tested with QuPath 4 #>  #> import qupath.lib.gui.tools.MeasurementExporter #> import qupath.lib.objects.PathCellObject #> import qupath.lib.objects.PathDetectionObject #>  #> // Get the list of all images in the current project #> def project = getProject() #> def imagesToExport = project.getImageList() #>  #> // Separate each measurement value in the output file with a tab ("  ") #> def separator = "," #>  #> // Choose the columns that will be included in the export #> // Note: if columnsToInclude is empty, all columns will be included #> def columnsToInclude = new String[]{"Image", "Name", "Class","Centroid X um","Centroid Y um","Nucleus: Area", "Nucleus: DAPI mean","Nucleus: E-Cadherin mean", "Nucleus: Cleaved caspase 3 mean", "Cell: Area","Cell: E-Cadherin mean", "Cell: Cleaved caspase 3 mean","Cytoplasm: E-Cadherin mean","Cytoplasm: Cleaved caspase 3 mean","Nucleus/Cell area ratio"} #>  #> // Choose the type of objects that the export will process #> // Other possibilities include: #> //    1. PathAnnotationObject #> //    2. PathDetectionObject #> //    3. PathRootObject #> // Note: import statements should then be modified accordingly #> def exportType = PathCellObject.class

what: How to Add and Run Scripts in QuPath (v0.4 / v0.5+)
title: QuPath Setup and Filename Metadata Conventions
text: Open Script Editor: QuPath’s top menu bar, select Automate →\rightarrowShow script editor (Ctrl + [ Windows/Linux, Cmd + [ macOS). Click File →\rightarrowNew Script Editor paste cell detection & object classification script package README (save project’s scripts/ folder appears Automate →\rightarrowProject scripts). Run across images project via Run →\rightarrowRun project Script Editor menu. Script Editor, click File →\rightarrowOpen... select script_for_qupath.txt file generated generate_qupath_script() (paste new tab via File →\rightarrowNew). Replace <...> placeholders outputPath sample metadata. Click Run →\rightarrowRun (Ctrl + R / Cmd + R). MeasurementExporter already loops getProject().getImageList(), single Run →\rightarrowRun exports project images .csv file.

title: QuPath Setup and Filename Metadata Conventions
text: Make sure columnsToInclude array Groovy script always starts "Image" "Name": Image: full image name (including series number, e.g., (series 01)), string_parsing() uses extract experimental metadata. Name: QuPath object classification assigned segmented cell (example, "PathCellObject", "cCasp3", "EpCAM_E-Cadherin").

Create a dedicated config directory and write a custom config_drugsens.txt custom_cfg_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "custom_project_config") dir.create(custom_cfg_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)  writeLines(   c(     "# Custom marker relabeling map",     "list_of_relabeling = list(",     '  "PathCellObject" = "Stromal_DAPI_only",',     '  "EpCAM_E-Cadherin: cCASP3" = "Early_Apoptotic_Tumor",',     '  "EpCAM_E-Cadherin" = "Viable_Tumor",',     '  "cCASP3" = "Late_Apoptotic"',     ")"   ),   con = file.path(custom_cfg_dir, "config_drugsens.txt") )  # 2. title: drugsens — Automated Drug Sensitivity Analysis from QuPath Data
text: 1. Cell Detection & Object Classification Script (STAR Protocol) add run script latest versions QuPath (v0.4 / v0.5+): Open QuPath project go top menu bar: Automate →\rightarrowShow script editor (press Ctrl + [ Windows/Linux, Cmd + [ macOS). Script Editor window, click File →\rightarrowNew paste Groovy script (tip: can also save inside QuPath project’s scripts/ folder via File →\rightarrowSave ... always accessible Automate →\rightarrowProject scripts). Update <USER_DEFINED_PATH> <...> metadata placeholders, confirm channel names (DAPI, E-Cadherin, Cleaved Caspase 3) single-measurement classifiers match project. test currently open image, click Run →\rightarrowRun (Ctrl + R / Cmd + R). process entire project batch, select Run →\rightarrowRun project Script Editor menu bar, move images Selected column, click OK. 2. Measurement Export Script (Exporting .csv) cell detection classification finished across project, use second script export single-cell measurements .csv format expected drugsens: QuPath, go Automate →\rightarrowShow script editor, click File →\rightarrowNew paste script (click File →\rightarrowOpen... load script_for_qupath.txt file generated R generate_qupath_script()). Set outputPath desired destination path filename following <PID>_<TISSUE>_... naming convention, verify columnsToInclude (make sure "Image" "Name" always included). Script Editor menu bar, click Run →\rightarrowRun (Ctrl + R / Cmd + R). Note: Click Run →\rightarrowRun (Run project), MeasurementExporter automatically iterates images getProject().getImageList() exports one step.
code: /**  * This QuPath script will take a full image as an annotation  *  * 1. Change path to export data, line 41  * 2. Make sure that the channel order is DAPI, E-Cadherin, and Cleaved Caspase 3  *      a) if this is not the case, change line 38 (setChannelNames) accordingly  * 3. Your QuPath project must contain classifiers called "Cleaved Caspase 3" and "E-Cadherin"  *    If you do not have them, you can download them from our repository,  *    or create them yourself:  *      i) In a image, create a selection of the full image (run lines 52-59)  *      ii) Detect cells (run line 61)  *      iii) In the Annotation tab, create new classification classes (Add class) called "Cleaved Caspase 3" and "E-Cadherin"  *      iv) Create classifiers (from the menu Classify > Object Classification > Create single measurement classifier)  *      v) Name the new classifier "Cleaved Caspase 3", and use following parameters  *              Object filter = Detections (all)  *              Channel filter = Cleaved Caspase 3  *              Measurement = Nucleus: Cleaved Caspase 3 mean  *              Threshold = 200 (value may differ for your image)  *              Above threshold = Cleaved Caspase 3  *      vi) Name the new classifier "E-Cadherin", and use following parameters  *              Object filter = Detections (all)  *              Channel filter = E-Cadherin  *              Measurement = Nucleus: E-Cadherin mean  *              Threshold = 180 (value may differ for your image)  *              Above threshold = E-Cadherin  * 4. Select Run -> Run for project  *    It will go through all images in the project, run segmentation  *    & apply those 2 classifiers we set up before.  *  * Note:  *    You are encouraged to check and adjust the classifier before you run them on your own images.  *    For this, follow steps 3.i) - 3.vi)  */  import static qupath.lib.gui.scripting.QPEx.*  // Define the path for data export def path = '<USER_DEFINED_PATH>'  setImageType('FLUORESCENCE'); setChannelNames ('DAPI', 'E-Cadherin', 'Cleaved Caspase 3')  def name = getProjectEntry().getImageName() + '.txt' path = buildFilePath(path, '<PID>_<TISSUE>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<SAMPLE_DOC>_<TREATMENT_INITIALS>_<CONCENTRATION>_<CONCENTRATION_UNITS>_<REPLICA_OR_NOT>_<TUMOR_MARKER>_<APOPTOTIC_MARKER>') mkdirs(path) path = buildFilePath(path, name)  // Create a new rectangle annotation & add it to the hierarchy import qupath.lib.roi.RectangleROI import qupath.lib.objects.PathAnnotationObject def x_dim = getCurrentImageData().getServer().getWidth() def y_dim = getCurrentImageData().getServer().getHeight() def roi = new RectangleROI(0, 0, x_dim, y_dim) def annotation = new PathAnnotationObject(roi) addObject(annotation) setSelectedObject(annotation)  runPlugin('qupath.imagej.detect.cells.WatershedCellDetection', '{"detectionImage": "DAPI",  "requestedPixelSizeMicrons": 0.5,  "backgroundRadiusMicrons": 8.0,  "medianRadiusMicrons": 0.0,  "sigmaMicrons": 2,  "minAreaMicrons": 5.0,  "maxAreaMicrons": 500.0,  "threshold": 45.0,  "watershedPostProcess": true,  "cellExpansionMicrons": 7.5,  "includeNuclei": true,  "smoothBoundaries": true,  "makeMeasurements": true}') runObjectClassifier("Cleaved Caspase 3", "E-Cadherin")  saveAnnotationMeasurements(path) print 'Results exported to ' + path /**  * QuPath script to export measurements from all analysed images in a project  *  * 1. Define columns you would like to export (line 28)  * 2. In line 17, specify the path where to save your results  */  import qupath.lib.gui.tools.MeasurementExporter import qupath.lib.objects.PathCellObject import qupath.lib.objects.PathDetectionObject import qupath.lib.objects.PathAnnotationObject import qupath.lib.objects.PathRootObject  // Choose your *full* output path def outputPath = "<USER_DEFINED_PATH>/<PID>_<TISSUE>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<SAMPLE_DOC>_<TREATMENT_INITIALS>_<CONCENTRATION>_<CONCENTRATION_UNITS>_<REPLICA_OR_NOT>_<TUMOR_MARKER>_<APOPTOTIC_MARKER>.csv"  // Get the list of all images in the current project def project = getProject() def imagesToExport = project.getImageList()  // Separate each measurement value in the output file with "," def separator = ","  // Choose the columns that will be included in the export // Note: if 'columnsToInclude' is empty, all columns will be included def columnsToInclude = new String[]{"Image", "Name", "Class","Centroid X um","Centroid Y um","Nucleus: Area", "Nucleus: DAPI mean","Nucleus: E-Cadherin mean", "Nucleus: Cleaved caspase 3 mean", "Cell: Area","Cell: E-Cadherin mean", "Cell: Cleaved caspase 3 mean","Cytoplasm: E-Cadherin mean","Cytoplasm: Cleaved caspase 3 mean","Nucleus/Cell area ratio"}  // Choose the type of objects that the export will process // Other possibilities include: //    1. PathAnnotationObject //    2. PathDetectionObject //    3. PathRootObject // Note: import statements should then be modified accordingly def exportType = PathCellObject.class  def outputFile = new File(outputPath)  // Create the measurementExporter and start the export def exporter  = new MeasurementExporter()         .imageList(imagesToExport)            // Images from which measurements will be exported         .separator(separator)                 // Character that separates values         .includeOnlyColumns(columnsToInclude) // Columns are case-sensitive         .exportType(exportType)               // Type of objects to export         .exportMeasurements(outputFile)        // Start the export process  print "Done!"

title: Plot some QC plots to define that everything ran correctly — get_QC_plots
code: get_QC_plots(   .data,   patient_column_name = "PID",   colors = unname(drugsens_palette),   save_plots = FALSE,   folder_name = NULL,   x_plot_var = "Treatment_complete",   isolate_a_specific_patient = NULL,   compare_to_control = FALSE,   control_treatment_name = "Control",   stat_method = c("wilcox", "t.test"),   p_adjust_method = "BH",   pvalue_label = c("p.adj.signif", "p.signif", "p.adj.format", "p.format") )

title: Plot some QC plots to define that everything ran correctly — get_QC_plots
text: .data preprocessed data (running make_count_dataframe() change_data_format_to_longer()) merged data.frame visualized patient_column_name PID's column name merged data.frame (defaults "PID") colors character vector colors supply personalize plot, defaults unname(drugsens_palette) (8-color CVD-safe palette). save_plots Boolean value indicating plots saved (default FALSE) folder_name Directory plots saved save_plots = TRUE. Defaults file.path(tempdir(), "figures") NULL. x_plot_var string indicating treatment's full name QC plots (default "Treatment_complete") isolate_a_specific_patient string indicating patient name isolate single plot case (default NULL) compare_to_control Logical, whether compute display statistical comparisons control_treatment_name within marker facet. Defaults FALSE. control_treatment_name Value x_plot_var identifying control/vehicle group compare_to_control = TRUE. Defaults "Control". stat_method Statistical test used compare_to_control = TRUE: "wilcox" (default) "t.test". p_adjust_method Multiple-testing correction method passed stats::p.adjust() across treatments within marker facet. Supports "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, default), "bonferroni", "holm", "fdr", "hochberg", "hommel", "", "none". pvalue_label Format p-value annotations: "p.adj.signif" (adjusted *, **, ***, ns, default), "p.signif" (unadjusted), "p.adj.format", "p.format".

title: Plot some QC plots to define that everything ran correctly — get_QC_plots
text: save_plots = FALSE, returns ggplot object (single patient plotted) named list ggplot objects (keyed patient ID). save_plots = TRUE, invisibly returns named list ggplot objects saving PDFs disk.

what: Normalize marker values to percent of control — normalize_to_control
title: Normalize marker values to percent of control — normalize_to_control
text: Expresses marker measurement (biological target-cell viability / cell-death metric computed user-selected dead_markers viable_markers / total_markers) percentage mean control (untreated/vehicle) value within patient. standard first step building dose response curves estimating \(\mathrm{IC}_{50}\) drug sensitivity assays, following Labrosse et al. (2024) doi:10.1016/j.xpro.2024.103274. dead_markers (e.g. "cCASP3") viable_markers (e.g. "EpCAM_E-Cadherin") total_markers (e.g. c("EpCAM_E-Cadherin", "cCASP3")) supplied, normalize_to_control() first computes well/image: dead_cells_ratio: sum dead_markers total_target_cells_ratio: sum total_markers (living target cells + dying cells, excluding unrelated DAPI-stromal cells) viable_cells_ratio: total_target_cells_ratio - dead_cells_ratio dead_fraction: dead_cells_ratio / total_target_cells_ratio viable_fraction: 1 - dead_fraction (viable_cells_ratio / total_target_cells_ratio) normalizes chosen response_metric ("viability" "cell_death") matched control_treatment_name group.

title: Normalize marker values to percent of control — normalize_to_control
code: normalize_to_control(   .data,   control_treatment_name = "Control",   treatment_column_name = "Treatment",   group_by_columns = "PID",   value_columns = NULL,   pattern_column_markers = "_ratio_of_total_cells",   dead_markers = NULL,   viable_markers = NULL,   total_markers = NULL,   response_metric = c("viability", "cell_death"),   selected_treatments = NULL,   consensus_only = FALSE )

title: Normalize marker values to percent of control — normalize_to_control
text: .data data frame either wide format returned make_count_dataframe() long format returned change_data_format_to_longer(). control_treatment_name Value identifying control/vehicle wells treatment_column_name. Defaults "Control". treatment_column_name Column holding treatment label. Defaults "Treatment". group_by_columns Columns define comparable batch: control mean computed within combination columns. Defaults "PID". value_columns Columns normalize. NULL, uses "marker_positivity_ratio" present (long format), otherwise columns matching pattern_column_markers (wide format). pattern_column_markers Pattern used auto-detect marker columns wide format. Defaults "_ratio_of_total_cells". dead_markers Optional character vector marker name(s) representing dead/dying cells (e.g. "cCASP3" c("cCASP3", "E-Cadherin cCASP3")). Matches names without "_ratio_of_total_cells" suffix. viable_markers Optional character vector marker name(s) representing viable target/cancer cells (e.g. "EpCAM_E-Cadherin" "E-Cadherin"). multiple viable_markers dead_markers supplied, markers paired positionally length(viable_markers) == length(dead_markers); otherwise combinations evaluated alongside combined consensus panel. total_markers Optional character vector marker name(s) representing total target cell population (e.g. c("EpCAM_E-Cadherin", "cCASP3")). NULL dead_markers viable_markers provided, defaults unique(c(viable_markers, dead_markers)). response_metric Metric compute normalize dead_markers provided: "viability" (default, 1 - dead / total, starts 100% control decreases toward 0% cells die) "cell_death" (dead / total). selected_treatments Optional character vector treatment names keep (addition control_treatment_name). Defaults NULL (treatments). consensus_only Logical; multiple viable_markers dead_markers supplied consensus_only = FALSE (default), normalize_to_control() computes individual marker pair's readout well combined "Consensus (Combined)" readout across selected markers. Set consensus_only = TRUE return combined consensus readout.

title: Normalize marker values to percent of control — normalize_to_control
text: .data added column per normalized value: "_pct_of_control" wide format, single "pct_of_control" column long format. dead_markers supplied, also includes dead_cells_ratio, viable_cells_ratio, total_target_cells_ratio, dead_fraction, viable_fraction, is_consensus.

title: Normalize marker values to percent of control — normalize_to_control
code: # A patient with a control group and one drug at three doses df <- data.frame(   PID = "PID1",   Treatment = c("Control", "Control", "DrugA", "DrugA", "DrugA"),   cCASP3_ratio_of_total_cells = c(10, 10, 5, 20, 40) ) normalize_to_control(df) #>    PID Treatment cCASP3_ratio_of_total_cells #> 1 PID1   Control                          10 #> 2 PID1   Control                          10 #> 3 PID1     DrugA                           5 #> 4 PID1     DrugA                          20 #> 5 PID1     DrugA                          40 #>   cCASP3_ratio_of_total_cells_pct_of_control #> 1                                        100 #> 2                                        100 #> 3                                         50 #> 4                                        200 #> 5                                        400

what: Plot dose response curves from normalized data — plot_dose_response
title: Plot dose response curves from normalized data — plot_dose_response
text: Plots percent--control marker values drug concentration, standard dose response view drug sensitivity assays. Expects data already processed normalize_to_control(). Supports non-parametric LOESS smoothing (method = "loess"), 4-parameter log-logistic Hill curve fitting (method = "4pl"), linear trend lines (method = "linear").

title: Plot dose response curves from normalized data — plot_dose_response
code: plot_dose_response(   .data,   concentration_column_name = "Concentration1",   treatment_column_name = "Treatment",   patient_column_name = "PID",   control_treatment_name = "Control",   log_scale_x = TRUE,   method = c("loess", "4pl", "linear"),   show_ic50 = FALSE,   dead_markers = NULL,   viable_markers = NULL,   total_markers = NULL,   response_metric = c("viability", "cell_death"),   selected_treatments = NULL,   consensus_only = FALSE,   consensus_dispersion = c("cv", "rcvq", "rcv_mad", "sd", "se", "iqr", "mad", "none"),   show_cv = TRUE )

title: Plot dose response curves from normalized data — plot_dose_response
text: .data Data frame normalize_to_control() long format (must contain "pct_of_control", "marker_positivity", concentration column). concentration_column_name Column holding drug concentration. Defaults "Concentration1". treatment_column_name Column holding treatment label. Defaults "Treatment". patient_column_name Column holding patient ID. Defaults "PID". control_treatment_name Value identifying control/vehicle wells, excluded dose response curve. Defaults "Control". log_scale_x Logical, whether plot concentration log10 axis (usual view doses span orders magnitude). Defaults TRUE; rows non-positive concentration dropped TRUE. method Curve fitting method: "loess" (default), "4pl" (4-parameter log-logistic Hill model estimated via stats::optim()), "linear". "4pl" used, data frame estimated ic50, hill_slope, bottom, top parameters attached attr(plot, "ic50"). show_ic50 Logical; TRUE method = "4pl", draws vertical dashed reference line estimated IC50 concentration fitted curve. Defaults FALSE. dead_markers Optional character vector marker name(s) representing dead/dying cells (e.g. "cCASP3"). provided, normalize_to_control() called automatically compute target cell response plotting. viable_markers Optional character vector marker name(s) representing viable target/cancer cells (e.g. "EpCAM_E-Cadherin"). total_markers Optional character vector marker name(s) representing target cells (e.g. c("EpCAM_E-Cadherin", "cCASP3")). response_metric Metric compute dead_markers supplied: "viability" (default) "cell_death". selected_treatments Optional character vector drug treatment names plot (e.g. "Paclitaxel"). consensus_only Logical; multiple viable_markers dead_markers supplied, FALSE (default) plots individual panels marker pair plus "Consensus Viability (Combined)" panel attaches consensus IC50 table attr(plot, "consensus_ic50"). Set TRUE plot combined consensus panel. consensus_dispersion Coefficient variation dispersion metric compute per point Consensus panel (attached attr(plot, "consensus_cv") plotted error bars / point labels): "cv" (standard coefficient variation 100 * SD / Mean, default), "rcvq" (robust quartile CV 100 * 0.75 * IQR / Median), "rcv_mad" (robust MAD CV 100 * MAD / Median), "sd" (standard deviation), "se" (standard error), "iqr" (interquartile range), "mad" (median absolute deviation), "none". Note rcvq rcv_mad require multiple marker pairs/replicates per dose (informative >= 3 values per dose available). show_cv Logical; whether print per-point CV (selected consensus_dispersion value) Consensus panel. Defaults TRUE.

title: drugsens 0.2.0
text: normalize_to_control(): expresses marker values percentage control/vehicle group per patient, multi-marker apoptosis/viability scoring (dead_markers, viable_markers, total_markers, response_metric, consensus_only). plot_dose_response(): plots percent--control values drug concentration using LOESS (method = "loess"), 4-parameter log-logistic Hill curves (method = "4pl" show_ic50 option, attr(plot, "ic50") parameter table, multi-marker consensus IC50 attr(plot, "consensus_ic50")), linear trends (method = "linear"), optional per-point marker dispersion/CV (consensus_dispersion, show_cv, attr(plot, "consensus_cv")). plot_dose_response_heatmap(): treatment x concentration overview heatmap percent--control numerical concentration ordering optional tile value labels (show_values). plot_treatment_summary(): ranked bar chart mean percent--control per treatment standard error bars optional statistical comparisons Control (compare_to_control). plot_patient_heatmap(): patient x treatment overview heatmap percent--control optional tile value labels (show_values) statistical comparisons Control (compare_to_control). plot_normalization_before_after(): side--side raw-ratio vs. percent--control panels per marker. drugsens_theme() drugsens_palette: exported publication-ready ggplot2 theme 8-color CVD-safe categorical palette used across package figures. Optional statistical comparisons control (compare_to_control, stat_method, p_adjust_method defaulting "BH", pvalue_label) get_QC_plots(), plot_treatment_summary(), plot_patient_heatmap(). Four comprehensive vignettes (drugsens, qupath--metadata, quality-control-workflow, cohort--dose-response) pkgdown documentation website. Expanded testthat unit test suite covering counting, reshaping, control normalization, 4PL dose-response fitting, statistical comparisons, plotting functions.

title: drugsens 0.2.0
text: get_QC_plots() now returns ggplot object (single patient) named list ggplot objects (multiple patients) interactive vignette use. Improved label wrapping across plots biological acronyms (cCASP3, EpCAM) concentration units (uM, nM) remain intact. make_run_config() now immediately loads list_of_relabeling creating config_drugsens.txt first run.
